sentences.text:
In nut-shell,
shell, the facts emerging from record are that the petitioner was facing a trial for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 406, 420, 120-B 120 of IPC and in the abovementioned case, they were on bail,, but later on when they could not appear before the learned trial Court on 22.05.2025,
the learned trial Court cancelled the bail of the petitioner and issued warrants of arrest.

Thereafter,
on various occasions, petitioners non-bailable bailable warrants were issued, however, the same could not be executed as the petitioners petitioner had left for a foreign country country.

4. Subsequently, vide order dated 06.06.2025, the learned trial Court issued proclamation against the petitioner petitioners and the date for appearance fixed in the abovementioned proclamation was 15.07.2025.
On 12.06.2025, the statement of serving Constable was recorded and thereafter, by virtue of impugned order, the petitioners were declared proclaime proclaimed offenders.

5. Notice of motion.
6.
Mr. Eklavya Darshi, Deputy Advocate General, Punjab appears on behalf of respondent-State.
respondent Hence service of notice upon the State is hereby dispensed with.

7. Heard.
8.

It has been contended on behalf of petitioners that the learned trial Court has committed an error when without following due process, it declared the petitioners petitioner to be proclaimed person persons..

According to learned counsel for the petitioners, petitioner , one of the basic steps to be taken during the course of proclamation was the reading of proclamation at a public place,
CRM-M-4553 4553-2026 (O&M) 3 and that in the present case, the executing Constable had not publicly read the proclamation at a public place.

9. In addition to above, it has been alleged by the petitioner petitioners that becausee of defective procedure adopted by the learned trial Court, in declaring the petitioners petitioner to be proclaimed offender offenders,, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

10. Per contra,, the learned State Counsel has argued that the petitioner are the person, who,
violated the condition petitioners conditions of bail with impunity, and took the law in their own hands and went abroad without caring for the criminal proceedings pending against them them.

As per learned State Counsel, since the petitioners petitioner themselves opted not to appear before the Court, and remained absent, now they cannot draw benefit of any technical defect, defect which could not be followed in declaring the petitioner petitioners to be proclaimed offenders..

sentences.text: The record has been perused carefully.

12. A perusal of the record shows that the petitioner petitioners have placed on record the copy of statement of the Executing Constable recorded by the learned trial Court, before declaring the petitioner petitioners to be proclaimed offenders..

The statement of Executing Constable, namely Dana Ram dated 12.06.2025 reads as under:-
"Stated Stated that the proclamation requiring the appearance of accused Jagtar Singh and Balwinder Kaur dated 09.06.2025 was handed over to me for compliance by the SHO PS Sirhind.
On 10.06.2025 I went to the given address and at the house of said accused and published proclamation at the house.
The second copy of the same was affixed at place where the Auto and bus stopped.
The third copy is fixed at the notice board of CRM-M-4553 4553-2026 (O&M) 4 the Hon'ble Court.

My report is Ex.PX/1 & Ex.PX over which I identify my signature at pt.A the proclamation is Ex.PY/1 & PY.'
14.

A bare perusal of the above above-mentioned mentioned statement of the Executing Constable shows that the above above-named named Executing Constable had not ot publicly read the contents of the proclamation.
The order dated 15.07.2025 shows that on the basis of above abovementioned mentioned statement of the Executing Constable, the petitioners petitioner have ve been declared proclaimed persons.
persons 15.

sentences.text: With regard rd to mandatory nature of above abovementioned mentioned procedure, it has been repeatedly observed by this Court, that the compliance of abovementioned provisions of Section 82(2) of CrPC iss mandatory in nature.

It has also been held that in case the above process is not followed in CRM-M-4553 4553-2026 (O&M) 5 letter and spirit, the impugned order declaring a person to be a proclaimed offender/proclaimed person is defective.

17. In addition to above, it is also relevant to mention here that the statement ement of executing Constable nowhere nowhere depicts that the proclamation was read over at a public place in the area where the petitioner ordinarily resides, as prescribed under Section 82(2)(i)(a) 82(2)(i)(a)
Cr.P.C., and the impugned order declaring the abovesaid abovesaid person to be a proclaimed person/proclaimed offender is defective and not sustainable in the eyes of law.

18. This Court in the cases of 'Jarnail Jarnail Singh v. State of Punjab & Anr.' CRM-M-27944 CRM of 2024 and 'Gagandeep Gagandeep Singh v. State of Punjab' Punjab CRM-M-50704 50704-2024, it has been observed that if a proclamation is not read at a conspicuous place of the town or village in which such person ordinarily resides, as prescribed under Section 82(2) 82(2)(i)(a), the order rder declaring the above said person to be a proclaimed person/proclaimed offender is defective and not sustainable in the eyes of law.

Resultantly, the present petition is hereby allowed and the impugned order dated 15.07.2025 passed by the learned trial Court is hereby quashed.
quashed CRM-M-4553 20.
It is however made clear that this order is with regard to legality of proclamation only.

Since the petitioner petitioners had jumped the bail and their bail has been cancelled and bonds have been forfeited to the State, the order of learned trial Court with regard to cancellation of bail and issuance of warrant of arrest against the petitioners petitioner shall remain intact, and therefore, in case the petitioner surrender before the learned trial Court, the learned trial Court petitioners will be at liberty to take take the petitioner petitioners into custody or proceed under Section 491 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (erstwhile Section 446 Cr.P.C).
However, However in case the petitioner petitioners surrender and file an application for bail, bail the same be disposed of expeditiously, and in any case within a period of seven days.
